text:
maya: Customer acme-org opened SUP-8591 — SSO started failing intermittently right after IdP cert rotation. Their browser shows a login loop and our SAML logs show 'InvalidSignature' and XML parse errors. Anyone seen this pattern?

sam: I can take a look. Do we have the raw metadata we fetched? Our fetch logs should show headers + body size.

maya: Pasting what we logged from our metadata fetcher — header snippet: `HTTP/1.1 200 OK\nContent-Type: application/xml\nContent-Encoding: br\nContent-Length: 768\n` But the body size we wrote to disk is tiny and the XML parser errors on parse. When I curl the URL from my laptop I get a normal XML.

lucy: Hmm. If Content-Encoding: br and the client didn't decompress, the cache could have stored compressed bytes. Our metadata parser expects raw XML and will fail loudly, then we keep using cached certs. Any chance the CDN served compressed payload but stripped the header on the edge?

sam: Looking at the fetcher logs: `fetch_metadata() -> 200, body_read=92 bytes, decode_error: unexpected EOF while inflating` — that suggests we attempted to gunzip or deflate but failed on Brotli bytes. Our http client normally auto-decodes gzip/deflate; Brotli support depends on client and headers. If the CDN returned brotli but dropped Content-Encoding sometimes, our client saved the compressed blob as-is.

maya: Repro steps I used: `curl -H "Accept-Encoding: br" -sS https://idp.acme/idp/metadata -D - -o /tmp/md.br` then `file /tmp/md.br` shows "Brotli compressed data". If you accidentally pass that file into `xmllint --noout /tmp/md.br` it fails with parse errors similar to what we saw.

lucy: Short-term mitigation: I purged the metadata cache for acme-org via the admin console and forced an immediate refetch (we added a manual refresh button). Please ask the customer to retry SSO. :white_check_mark:

sre-bot: metadata cache purged for acme-org by maya at 2025-03-17T14:04Z (action: manual-refresh).

maya: Customer confirmed SSO works after the purge. They said the issue was intermittent (likely CDN edge). We'll keep ticket open while we push a durable fix.

sam: Follow-up work: add Brotli-aware handling in the metadata fetcher, and add a guard that detects non-XML cached payloads and forces a re-fetch. I'll open an infra issue and add an e2e test. (GH: infr/fetcher#3214)

lucy: Assigning to eng-infra to implement the fix, @sam please coordinate tests. I'll prepare a quick patch to detect compressed payloads and to log a clear error so support can triage faster.
